$comment: Whether a failed request is worth another attempt, as every implementation must answer it. `rules`: the four named rules, each for one context, asked about a response's `status` and the request's `method`; a row that omits either field leaves it unstated. `boot`: a boot pass or a bus request, where the peer is usually seconds from ready. `job`: a job's retry budget, where not retrying discards paid work. `transport`: an HTTP client that can renew its token; a 401 is retried on any method, everything else only on a method that cannot cause a second effect. `refresh`: exchanging a refresh token at its issuer, where the issuer's answer is the verdict and its absence never is. `retryAfter`: the wait a `Retry-After` header states, in milliseconds, when it gives whole seconds, the form the gateway sends; `ms` is null when it states none. TypeScript runs this in packages/core (retry-agreement.test.ts) against RETRY_RULES and retryAfterMs. Rust runs it in packages/sdk-rust (tests/retry_cases.rs). Python runs it in packages/sdk-python (tests/test_retry.py), for the three rules the SDK keeps, and in apps/worker (tests/test_retry_job_rule.py), for `job`, which is the worker's.

rules.why: 429 is the server saying not now
503 is a promise to recover
504 is a promise to recover
500 is an unclassified fault: replaying it inside a boot pass re-runs whatever broke it
401 means the gateway is up and refused
400 will be refused again
408 is a timeout
429 is the server saying not now
500 is retried here where boot refuses it: the alternative is discarding paid work
503 is a promise to recover
400 will be refused again
401 will be refused again
404 will be refused again
a 401 on a POST is retried: the request was refused, not processed
a 401 on a GET is retried
a 401 with no method stated is retried: 401 does not depend on the method
a 502 on a POST is not retried: it may already have been processed, and a repeat writes twice
a 502 on a GET is retried
a 503 on a PUT is retried: PUT is idempotent
a 500 on a DELETE is retried: DELETE is idempotent
a 429 on a POST is not retried by this rule
a 429 on a GET is retried
a 413 on a GET is retried
the method is read in any case
a 404 on a GET will be refused again
a 500 with no method stated is not retried: unstated reads as unsafe
no status is not retried by this rule
no response at all is the network, not the issuer: the session survives a lost packet
400 is the issuer refusing the grant: terminal on the first answer
401 is the issuer refusing the client
404 on the token endpoint is a misconfiguration, not a promise to recover: unclassified is terminal
408 is not now
429 is not now
500 is retried here where boot refuses it: one idempotent exchange has no side effect to replay
503 is not now

retryAfter.why: zero seconds is a stated wait of none
surrounding whitespace is not part of the value
an empty header states no wait
the HTTP-date form is not the form the gateway sends
a fraction is not whole seconds
a negative number is not a wait
